Currently, it appears that all templates (excluding spaces) begin with the first two characters of the sorted faces. Consider revising two or more of the case pairs to account for scenarios where this does not hold true. For example, when the first two characters of the sorted faces are opposites and therefore cannot be adjacent in a T-shaped template.

Thanks.

✅ Approved the contribution.
Comment: He deserves it.

This puzzle looks interesting in its idea but is very tedious to implement.
A large part of the tediousness lies in the unhandy input format.
The ascii drawings could be replaced by data given directly like that:

3 adjacent faces: A B C
2 adjacent faces: A B
2 adjacent faces: B C

Designing good algorithm and data structure is enjoyable. Using lots of effort in data formatting during I/O is not quite a fun. Just my personal opinion.

Hey CodinGamer! Your contribution has unfortunately not been moderated on time and will temporarily be removed from the system... But no worries! You can republish it anytime to give it another chance! :)

Goal
* Please change "that shows" to "that show" (the verb refers to "images", right?).

* Consider changing "of the fully constructed die that shows the geometric orientations of some of the faces" to "that show some of the faces of the fully constructed die".

Input
* Line 1: Consider simplifying as:
{{6}} face labels used on the die, in no particular order

Output
* Consider simplifying the first point:
Two die templates are <<equal>> if their folded dice can be rotated to match.

Constraints
* Please add constraints for [[W]] and [[H]].

Cases
* You are probably aware that [[W]] is incorrect in more than half of the cases.

* Some cases include face labels that are also used as edge characters in the 3D images (/, \, |, +, -, v). These require special attention. Currently:
  • /: Validators 7, 9, 17
  • \: Validator 8, Test 18
  • |: Test 19, Validator 20
  • +: Test 21
  • -: Validator 14, Test 24
  • v: Validator 3, Test 19, Validator 23
  "/" doesn't appear in tests and "+" doesn't appear in validators. The cases should be adjusted to ensure proper coverage.

Thanks.

Hey @java_coffee_cup, just to clarify, is your feedback pertaining to the ASCII representation of the die faces? I.e., this part:

  (1)  |  (2)  |  (3)
 \ A / |       | --+--
  \ /  | / A \ |   |  
   v   | +---+ | B | C
 B | C | | B | |   |  
   |   |       | --+--

Since these three representations are fixed, I thought it would be simple enough to infer how to parse the representations without having to parse the entire ASCII art. My solution essentially checks the top-left corner of each 5x5.

It's definitely not as easy to parse as the input format you're suggesting, but I don't think it's that big / tedious of an I/O challenge as you suggest. Plus, I think the visual aid makes it ever so slightly trickier to treat representations (2) and (3) as one and the same.
Thank you for your quick response too! 👍

I'm not going to suggest changing the puzzle's state again like last time, since I'm not completely sure whether the latest approvals count as abuse or not. I'll leave that decision up to you.

That said, since I haven't approved any contributions in a while, I wanted to ask: do you receive any XP for being one of the three approvers on a successfully approved clash or puzzle? If so, how much XP do you get in each case?

No XP is received for approving or rejecting a puzzle for a long time. (If I remember correctly there was a modest XP a few years ago, but not anymore.)
But there is quest map item for doing a puzzle approval/rejection.
For the puzzle contributors there are still some XP (I don't remember 150 or 250 XP, it has been years since my last contribution) and another quest map item as well.
Thanks for the info!
